chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-A'la ibn Manzur, the freedman of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The woman who requests divorce, if she says to her husband, 'Divorce me,' and he divorces her by her command and with her consent, then it is a final divorce, and there is no right of return for him over her, and there is no inheritance between them, and she observes the waiting period from him for three months or three menstrual periods.

And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said regarding the man who divorces his wife with a divorce in which he does not have the right of return: 'She has become permanently divorced from him, and there is no inheritance between them during the waiting period.'

key_terms.الرَّجْعَةُ: The right of return (to take back the wife without a new marriage contract)
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: The waiting period observed by a divorced or widowed woman
key_terms.الْقُرُوءُ: Menstrual periods (used as a measure for the waiting period)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَأْمَرَةُ: A woman who requests divorce from her husband
key_terms.طَلَاقٌ بَائِنٌ: A final/separable divorce where the husband cannot easily take her back without a new contract

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status and waiting period for a woman who initiates her own divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of *Khula* (divorce initiated by the wife), establishing it as a final separation (*Talaq al-Bain*) where the husband forfeits the right of revocation (*Raj'ah*). It further specifies that mutual inheritance is suspended during the waiting period (*Iddah*), a ruling derived from the principle that the marital bond is effectively severed upon the wife's consent and the husband's acceptance. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that *Khula* carries the same finality as a standard divorce regarding inheritance and revocation rights.
